key_insight: The paper uses physics-informed neural networks to optimize single-qubit quantum gates at the full evolution level, jointly learning control fields, state trajectories, and gate duration under the Bloch equation.
engineering_relevance: This makes quantum control more interpretable and hardware-adaptable by exposing physically meaningful trajectories and localized errors instead of only pulse amplitudes.
method: PINN represents the controlled qubit evolution directly via the Bloch equation.
The network jointly learns pulse shape, Bloch-state path, and total operation time.
A feedback step refines localized geometric-path errors for a geometric gate while keeping fidelity high.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful recovery of physically organized evolutions for rotation gates and reduced residual path error for a geometric gate without a prescribed pulse ansatz or duration sweep.
watch_item: The approach may require careful constraint handling and validation on real hardware, since learned trajectories can be sensitive to model mismatch and implementation noise.
paper_title: Evolution-Level Quantum Optimal Control of Single-Qubit Gates with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
